statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail remains in the low band: December NQ sits mid-band at 31,479.25 inside an 89.75-point overnight range, 48 points off its low, with VIX at 15.01 and no persistent one-way structure observable.
recommendation: Tail at 10% maps to EA_ON for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. The published forecast carries a WATCH band across the 17:00-20:00 UTC sequence on 7 October, covering the 10-year note auction, the September FOMC minutes and the following power hour, where Tail is modelled conditionally at 21-23%.
headline: NQ holds a shallow 90-point overnight band mid-range; Tail stays low ahead of the September FOMC minutes
body: The cash Nasdaq-100 closed 6 October at 31,224.69, up 148.24 points or 0.48%, after printing a fresh 52-week high at 31,361.37 and then fading to finish nearer the 31,208.20 session low. Overnight, December NQ futures trade 31,479.25, down 4.00 points or 0.01%, inside an 89.75-point band running 31,431.25 to 31,521.00 after an open at 31,510.00. Price now sits mid-band, 48 points above the low and 41.75 below the high, so the hour supplies two-sided retracement rather than repeated extension after failed pullbacks. The band is roughly 0.29% of the index. VIX is 15.01, down 3.29% from a 15.52 close, and December ES trades 7,879.00, up 0.06%, inside a 9.50-point range of 7,875.00 to 7,884.50. Cross-asset evidence conflicts rather than aligns: Asian cash has turned softer, with the Nikkei 225 at 70,156.49, down 0.75%, after closing 6 October at 70,683.98, and the Hang Seng at 24,151.90, down 0.53%, while US index futures hold flat. Under the published calibration that conflict raises Stress ahead of Tail. The macro backdrop stays restrictive. The H.15 release of 6 October shows 5 October constant-maturity yields at 4.84% for the 2-year, 5.31% for the 10-year and 5.66% for the 30-year, with the effective federal funds rate at 3.88%; the 10-year settled near 5.27% on 6 October after its highest closing level in 24 years the prior session, and the 30-year sits close to 2002 levels. WTI trades 90.19, up 0.84% from an 89.44 close, and Brent near 101.44, up 0.85%, with an active Strait of Hormuz tanker campaign as the supply channel. Reporting on 6 October notes at least seven tanker incidents in the preceding week and at least one attack daily since 2 October, while roughly 40% of Middle East crude exports already bypass the strait and late-September export volumes of 18.3 to 18.6 million barrels a day matched or exceeded pre-war levels. That makes the energy risk chronic and partly mitigated rather than a fresh discontinuity, which places it in Stress and Confidence rather than Tail. The session's catalysts stack into a three-hour window. A 10-year note auction prices at 17:00 UTC into that 5.31% yield, and the minutes of the 15-16 September FOMC meeting follow at 18:00 UTC. Those minutes cover a unanimous 12-0 decision to raise the target range by 25 basis points to 3.75-4.00%, the first increase since 2023, and they pre-date the September employment report released 2 October showing payroll growth of 29,000 and an unemployment rate of 4.2%. Because that report and an August core PCE rate of 3.0% already cut futures-implied odds of an October hike from roughly 70% to about 20%, the minutes are backward-looking relative to current pricing, which limits their repricing scope without removing it. FOMC minutes remain structurally multi-stage, so the forecast raises conditional Tail to 23% for the 18:00 UTC hour and holds the WATCH band through the 19:00 UTC power hour into the 20:00 UTC cash close. Equity leadership remains concentrated: the S&P 500 closed 6 October at 7,818.93, up 0.58%, and the Nasdaq Composite at a record 27,599.79, its 23rd record close of 2026, with Nvidia and AMD both at all-time highs and Nvidia's market value approaching $6 trillion. Concentration of that kind is a Stress and Confidence input; it does not by itself establish the pathological price path that Tail measures. Shared Finviz context was read and found stale, dated 29 September with a partial collection status, so it was excluded and the assessment rests entirely on independently verified current sources. Current Tail of 10% therefore maps to EA_ON, Stress of 46% sits in the elevated band on rates, energy and event density, and Confidence of 88% reflects verified index, futures, volatility, yield, energy, cross-market, geopolitical and calendar evidence against one stale supplementary feed.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly slots carry published Claude assessments. Tail ran 8-13% through the Asian and European hours of 6 October, lifted through the US session to a 22% peak in the 15:00 UTC hour as the index pushed to a fresh 52-week high, then decayed back to 10-13% overnight as the advance faded into the close and the overnight band compressed. Stress held a narrow 45-48% elevated range throughout and Confidence stayed at 86-88%.
outlookSummary: The modelled path keeps Tail in the low band through the Asian and European hours, lifts it to 17-19% across the 13:30 UTC cash open and the first cash hours for opening-auction structure, and raises it into the mapped WATCH band at 21-23% across the 17:00-20:00 UTC sequence covering the 10-year note auction, the September FOMC minutes and the power hour into the cash close. Tail then decays back toward 11-12% overnight on the assumption that price discovery completes inside the cash session. Every value beyond the current clock-hour is conditional risk, not observed structure.
